requested.title: Server-controlled timestamps reach `new Date(ms).toISOString()` unvalidated, throwing an uncaught RangeError
Out-of-range server-supplied serverTs crashes `maruhi audit` with an unhandled RangeError
invalidValueMessage matches on substrings of `expected`, mis-describing future at-least/at-most params
Config load treats all read errors as "file does not exist", masking permission/IO failures
`maruhi key show` crashes with an unhandled RangeError on an out-of-range server timestamp

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Verified in the current tree. `apps/cli/src/invite.ts:267-269` is `new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0,16)...` and is called at L254 (`invite create`) and L734 (`invite list`, twice per row) on `issued.expiresAtMs` / `row.createdAtMs` / `row.expiresAtMs`. Those fields come off the wire: `packages/api-schema/src/invites-api.ts` declares `createdAtMs`/`expiresAtMs` as bare `Schema.Number` (L71-72, L81) with no finite or range check. I confirmed in the pinned effect build (`effect@4.0.0-beta.107/dist/Schema.js:1737-1743`) that `Schema.Number` is `make(SchemaAST.number)` and explicitly does NOT reject non-finite values — `Schema.Finite` (L4162-4167) is the checked variant and is not used here. So any server-supplied value with |ms| > 8.64e15 (a plain finite JSON number like 1e17 suffices; `1e400` → Infinity also works) yields an Invalid Date and `toISOString()` throws `RangeError`. The throw is a synchronous throw inside `Effect.gen`, so it becomes a defect, not a typed `CliError`. One correction to the finding's impact claim: the defect does not escape as a raw stack trace — `runEffectCli` wraps the command in `Effect.exit` and `reportFailure` renders defects by type name only (`failure.ts:internalErrorKind`, `cli.ts:119-124`), so the user sees 'internal error (RangeError)' and a non-zero exit. The functional impact stands: `invite create` prints the one-time link at L252 and then dies before the 'shown only once / hand it over person-to-person / then member add' guidance, and `invite list` aborts on a single bad row, which is the acceptance-verification path `member add` depends on. Since the server is untrusted in this project's threat model (the CLI already sanitizes every server-supplied string via `displayText`), a malicious server can deterministically break these commands. Real but low-impact: availability/UX and a typed-error-discipline violation, not a confidentiality break — BUG severity is right.

Same defect class, independently confirmed at a different location, so not a duplicate (different file, different code path). `apps/cli/src/audit.ts:187-189` `formatTs` does `new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0,19)` and is called unconditionally at L265 inside `formatEventLine` on `event.serverTs`. I checked `packages/api-schema/src/audit-api.ts:77`: `serverTs: Schema.Number` — unbounded, unlike the PositiveInt-typed `seq`/`epoch`/`chainSeq`, and `clientTs` (L78) is likewise an unchecked optional number. As established for F1, `Schema.Number` in the pinned effect build accepts non-finite and out-of-range values, so a server row with `serverTs: 1e20` makes `toISOString()` throw `RangeError`. `formatEventLine` is a pure function called from the rendering paths for `audit` / `audit invites` / `audit self` and the mirror rendering used by `audit verify`, all inside `Effect.gen` with no surrounding `try`/`tryPromise`, so it surfaces as an Effect defect rather than a typed `CliError`. As with F1, the defect is caught at the top level and printed as 'internal error (RangeError)' with a non-zero exit rather than a bare stack trace, so the 'stack trace' phrasing is slightly overstated — but the outcome is the same: the audit-reading command, which exists precisely to let an operator detect a misbehaving server, can be disabled by that same server with one malformed row. Confirmed, BUG severity.

I read `cli-formatter.ts` fully and traced the upstream error construction in `effect/dist/unstable/cli/Param.js`. The 'at most' string only ever originates at Param.js:1424, inside `parseOptionVariadic` — the FLAG path — as the fixed text `at most N value(s)`. The argument path, `parseArgumentVariadic` (Param.js:1380-1402), enforces `max` by simply stopping consumption (`while (currentArgs.length > 0 && count < maxValue)`) and only ever emits the `at least` variant when `count < min`. So `Argument.atMost(1)` can never produce an 'at most' InvalidValue — the surplus positional becomes an `UnexpectedArgument` instead, which routes to `unexpectedArgumentMessage`. That kills the finding's core hypothetical: the two existing `Argument.atMost(1)` declarations (`effect-cli.ts:394` rotation-dismiss `variable`, `:612` member-add) already cannot mis-trigger the flag-duplication message. On the 'at least' side, I grepped the whole CLI: `Argument.atLeast(1)` appears only in `runCommandArgument()` (`effect-cli.ts:304`), shared by `run` and `ci run`, and no `Flag.atLeast` exists anywhere — so the hardcoded RUN_COMMAND_REQUIRED reply is correct for every reachable case today, not merely by accident of ordering. The secondary concern (a user-typed value containing the literal 'at least' reaching `expected`) is bounded: for schema failures upstream builds `expected` as `Schema validation failed: ${error.message}` (Param.js:1288) with the typed value carried separately in `value`, and even in the worst case the branch returns a fixed authored string, so there is no leakage — only a possible misdirected message for a value the user typed themselves. This is a maintainability/robustness note about a future declaration, not a present defect; the finding itself is stated in the future tense and rated low confidence. Marking false-positive for the current tree; hardening the dispatch to key off `error.kind` plus param name is still a reasonable cleanup.

Confirmed verbatim in the current file. `makeFileConfigStore.load` (config.ts:95-111) wraps `readFile(path, 'utf8')` in a bare `catch { return {}; }` whose comment says the intent is only the first-run/not-yet-created case, but which catches every errno — EACCES, EISDIR, ELOOP, EIO — indistinguishably. I verified the two downstream consequences. (1) Callers get `{}`: `configGet` (effect-cli.ts:1943) prints an empty line and server-origin resolution reports 'No server URL is configured…', pointing the user at config they already set. (2) More seriously, `configSet` (effect-cli.ts:1950-1971) deliberately pipes `store.load` through `Effect.catch` to emit 'Warning: … — discarding the existing config and recreating it with only this key' before rebuilding the file — but on an unreadable-yet-writable config the load takes the SUCCESS path with `{}`, so that warning never fires and `store.save` (which writes a temp file and renames over the target, requiring only directory write permission) silently destroys the user's other settings. The finding's own citation checks out as evidence of intended discipline: `floor-log.ts:807-813` defines `isFileMissingError` gating strictly on `code === 'ENOENT'` and rethrows otherwise (L856-860), exactly the pattern missing here. This is not attacker-controlled — it needs a local permission/ownership anomaly — so it is a correctness and silent-data-loss bug, not a security issue, and it also conflicts with the CLAUDE.md rule against `catch` blocks that swallow errors. BUG severity is correct.

Confirmed at `apps/cli/src/keygen.ts:171-173`: `formatDateUtc` is `new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0,10)`, called at L159 on `status.updatedAtMs`. I checked the schema: `packages/api-schema/src/auth-api.ts:111` declares `updatedAtMs: Schema.NullOr(Schema.Number)` — unbounded, and as established the pinned `Schema.Number` accepts non-finite and out-of-range values. So a server returning `{registered: true, updatedAtMs: 1e17}` makes `toISOString()` throw `RangeError` inside the `Effect.gen`, becoming a defect rather than a typed `CliError`. The contrast the finding draws is real and is what makes this a genuine bug rather than a nit: the surrounding code is deliberately defensive — the `recoveryStatus` call is wrapped in `Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(null))` at L149-151 specifically so that a failure to reach the server degrades to 'recovery: could not be checked' and never fails `key show`, whose actual job is displaying LOCAL key material (L137-144). A malformed timestamp bypasses that deliberate degradation and kills the command after it has already printed the local key info, replacing the intended output with 'internal error (RangeError)' and a non-zero exit (top-level defect handling in `cli.ts:119-124` / `failure.ts:internalErrorKind`, so no raw stack trace — the finding slightly overstates that detail). Under this project's untrusted-server threat model this is server-triggerable at will. Availability/UX plus a typed-error-discipline violation; BUG is the right severity.
